jobs.title: Senior Officer, AI Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General, and has its Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. IFRC has five regional offices in Africa, Asia Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas. IFRC also has country cluster delegations and country delegations throughout the world. Together, the Geneva Headquarters and the field structure (regional, cluster and country) comprise the IFRC Secretariat.

IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

Background to the position

In virtually all countries, people increasingly rely on and expect a diverse range of digital services (e.g., through their mobile devices) to interact with local government, companies, and community organizations and services. This disruption is already happening to humanitarian assistance. Yet, the Digital Divide remains a persistent and significant challenge at both national and local levels.

The need for a successful and large-scale digital transformation is urgent. And Digitally Transforming the IFRC and its 191 members is a complex process which requires collaborative action and support across the membership. Therefore, the IFRC recently developed a Digital Transformation Strategy which was approved by the IFRC Governing Board in May 2021.  

The Digital Transformation Department (DTD) has full leadership responsibility for the implementation of the digital transformation strategy and the positive impact it will have on the 191 National Society members of the IFRC. The DTD provides strategic leadership and guides the IFRC Secretariat as well as the members network to adapt and innovate humanitarian services, drawing on digital services, data-enabled decision-making, and other opportunities for digital transformation in support of the IFRC’s Strategy 2030. In addition, the DTD is responsible for the development and implementation of business transformation, information technology and digitalization services throughout the IFRC Secretariat, thereby supporting the same transformation in 191 NSs, setting the vision, and drawing stakeholders together on this digital journey. 

Job Purpose

The incumbent reports to the AI and Data management unit (“AI & Data unit”), that is accountable to the Director of the DTD. The other units and teams reporting to the DT Director include the Enterprise Architecture, Strategy & Planning unit, the Digital development and management unit, the Infrastructure & Security Team and the Global Service Desk and Endpoint Management team. Under the leadership of the Director, these units and teams serve as members of the global DTD management team, along with the CISO and Regional DT managers.

The AI & Data unit is responsible to deliver greater value from IFRC’s data, and ensures the development and implementation of IFRCs data and AI governance and strategy, in close collaboration with the IFRC’s Data Protection Office and through indirect management of data professionals in other departments. The unit oversees all data operations, data product lifecycles and manages the organisation’s data platform, as well as the coordination and support to AI initiatives.

The Senior Officer, AI Platform Engineering will also interact with internal and external AI and data experts, private sector, academia, external suppliers, vendors and consultants who are sourced to deliver AI-related activities.

Job Purpose

The Senior Officer, AI Platform Engineering builds and runs the shared platform that IFRC teams use to create AI solutions on Microsoft technologies. The role provisions and operates Azure AI services, supports colleagues who build agents in Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 Copilot, and makes it easy for teams to build AI that is secure, compliant and affordable.

The role puts into practice the IFRC security and governance standards, and works closely with developers, data protection colleagues and IT operations across the Secretariat.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Azure AI Platform Operations
Operate and maintain IFRC's Microsoft-based AI platforms and services (e.g. Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI and related Azure services, Copilot Studio and Power Platform) across development, testing and production environments.
Configure and maintain platform components and integrations to support the deployment and operation of AI applications and services.
Develop and maintain version-controlled infrastructure-as-code templates for AI platform resources, automate environment provisioning and identify and remediate configuration drift against approved baselines.
Manage model deployments, quotas and capacity, and track model retirements so that applications keep working when models are updated or withdrawn.
Ensure proper life-cycle management of AI related services.
Monitor platform availability, performance, resource utilization and operational costs, identifying opportunities for optimization.
Maintain resource tagging and usage attribution by team or solution, configure budget and abnormal-consumption alerts, provide cost and capacity forecasts, and coordinate the removal or resizing of unused resources with their owners.
Operate the AI gateway in Azure API Management, including authentication, rate limits per team, load balancing, and usage logging.
Troubleshoot platform and deployment issues, investigate incidents and implement corrective actions within the scope of the role.
Support for developers and makers
Build and maintain reusable templates, reference architectures and code samples for common patterns, such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents built with Foundry Agent Service or the Microsoft Agent Framework.
Support colleagues building AI applications and agents in Azure AI Foundry, building agents in Copilot Studio and extending Microsoft 365 Copilot, including environment setup, connectors and publishing.
Build and maintain the pipelines that connect AI services to IFRC data in SharePoint, Microsoft Fabric, Dataverse and other sources.
Onboard new teams to the platform, answer their technical questions and keep its documentation clear and current.
Collaborates with the team in developing and providing to the organization trainings and learning materials related to AI with a focus on platform and security.

Job Duties And Responsibilities (continued)

AI Workload Operations and Security
Build, maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines for AI applications and related platform components, including version control, automated testing, deployment and release management.
Develop and apply established operational practices for managing AI workloads, including appropriate resource allocation and environment configuration.
Implement established security configurations and operational procedures for AI workloads.
Implement and maintain approved Azure Policy and network security guardrails for AI services, including permitted deployment regions, private connectivity, restrictions on public access and approved authentication methods; monitor compliance and track exceptions through the agreed review process.
Monitor relevant Azure security alerts and recommendations affecting AI workloads (e.g. Defender for Cloud) and coordinate follow-up actions.
Apply established identity and access management practices for applications and workloads, including secure credential and secrets management using Azure Key Vault and Microsoft Entra ID.
Prepare the technical evidence needed for the release review of AI agents and services, and put agreed controls in place before go-live.
Support the implementation of data protection and security controls for AI solutions, including relevant Microsoft Purview configurations.
Contribute to technical security assessments and incident investigations related to AI workloads.
Configure Power Platform environments and data loss prevention (DLP) policies for Copilot Studio.
Documentation and Collaboration
Maintain technical documentation of Azure AI platforms and solutions, including deployment configurations, integrations, dependencies, operational procedures, data sources and data flows.
Collaborate with AI developers, data professionals and other technical stakeholders to ensure the reliable deployment and operation of AI solutions.
Ensure that AI platforms and workloads align with IFRC's infrastructure, security and operational standards.
Act as the first technical point of contact for operational questions and issues related to Azure AI platforms and deployed solutions.
Stay up to date with developments in Azure cloud technologies, platform engineering, DevOps and AI operations, and identify opportunities to improve platform reliability, automation, performance, cost efficiency and existing processes.

Duties applicable to all staff

Work actively towards the achievement of IFRC’s goals.
Abide by and work in accordance with the Red Cross and Red Crescent principles.
Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.

Education

Required

Degree in in computer science, information security, data science, or related field.

Preferred

Relevant Microsoft certifications, such as Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), Azure AI App and Agent Developer Associate (AI-103) or the earlier Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102), DevOps Engineer Expert (AZ-400) or Cloud and AI Security Engineer Associate (SC-500).

Experience

Required

Minimum 5 years of experience in cloud operations, DevOps, platform engineering or a related technical field.
Hands-on experience operating and maintaining applications and services in Microsoft Azure environments.
Experience developing and maintaining infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Bicep, Terraform) and automating environment provisioning.
Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (e.g. Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions) and managing deployment and release processes in production environments.
Experience with scripting and automation using Python and/or PowerShell
Experience with cloud monitoring, logging and troubleshooting tools (e.g. Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights).

Preferred

Experience operating or supporting AI/ML or generative AI applications in production environments.

jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

This position is open at any U.S. location near a Jacobs office. We intend to hire the best candidate regardless of geography.

About The Role

At Jacobs, we never settle — we push boundaries, elevate standards, and deliver with purpose. As a senior subject matter expert (SME) within our Data Center team, you’ll lead I&C engineering efforts across a portfolio of data center projects, including new builds and retrofits. As part of the vision of the I & C SME, you’ll drive the technical direction and ensure controls solutions meet the highest standards of performance and constructability.

You’ll serve as a key technical leader, guiding a portfolio of projects and coordinating closely with interdisciplinary engineering teams. You will mentor I&C leads and support the projects by meeting with clients and upper management as required, with the ability to speak directly to the status of various projects. Your expertise will shape project execution, influence design strategy, and strengthen our delivery excellence.

This role offers significant opportunities to expand your technical authority, mentor emerging talent, and grow your leadership presence as you help define the next generation of high-performance data center infrastructure. Your guidance will shape both design delivery and our Design-Build delivery methodology across a fast-growing hyperscale project portfolio.

Key Contributions

Provide quality reviews of complex projects spanning building automation systems (BAS), industrial control systems (ICS), SCADA, EPMS, and critical facility monitoring and control platforms for hyperscale data center facilities.
Lead complex controls architecture evaluations and guide the selection of appropriate control methodologies, network topologies, instrumentation strategies, and automation platforms to ensure robust, secure, code-compliant, and maintainable design solutions.
Develop and validate advanced control sequences, network communication architectures, and system integration strategies; establish controls design standards and mentor team members in best-practice automation, instrumentation, and controls engineering techniques.
Oversee critical calculations and analyses related to instrumentation sizing and selection, control valve applications, sensor accuracy and reliability, network capacity, alarm management, and controls integration; provide technical governance for schedules, design documentation, and interdisciplinary coordination.
Drive operational performance and reliability strategies through advanced monitoring, analytics, automated fault detection and diagnostics (FDD), energy optimization controls, and data-driven operational insights aligned with hyperscale owner objectives.
Partner with mechanical, electrical, civil, structural, and commissioning disciplines to ensure seamless integration of instrumentation and control systems throughout the project lifecycle, from concept design through commissioning, startup, and turnover.

At Jacobs, the world’s No. 1 design firm, you’ll lead industry-defining data center and advanced manufacturing projects with global impact.

Here's what you'll need

Ability to quickly identify complex technical challenges, develop practical solutions, communicate recommendations effectively, and direct junior and senior staff on best practices in controls engineering, automation architecture, and systems integration.
Understanding of the complexities of large contracts and different contract structures; ability to manage change orders and advocate for the engineering team regarding controls scope, integration responsibilities, and contractor liabilities.
Experience with the full spectrum of mission-critical facility control systems, including BAS, PLC-based control systems, SCADA platforms, EPMS integration, critical environmental monitoring systems, mechanical systems controls, and data center operational analytics, with the ability to communicate effectively with executive stakeholders on any subject without advance notice.
Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Instrumentation Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related engineering discipline.
15+ years of professional experience in instrumentation, controls, or automation engineering, with 5 or more years of demonstrated depth in mission-critical and/or data center facility design.
Registered Professional Engineer (PE) required.
Proficiency with controls and automation platforms such as Siemens, Schneider Electric, Johnson Controls, Honeywell, Rockwell Automation, Aveva/Wonderware, Ignition, Tridium Niagara, or equivalent systems.
Knowledge of industrial and building communication protocols including BACnet, Modbus TCP/IP, OPC UA, EtherNet/IP, DNP3, SNMP, and MQTT.
Knowledge of CAD and BIM platforms including Revit.
Knowledge and application of relevant industry standards and codes, including NFPA 70 (NEC), NFPA 72, NFPA 110, ISA-5.1, ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Standards, ASHRAE Guideline 36, ASHRAE TC 9.9 recommendations, Uptime Institute guidance, and other data center industry standards.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Microsoft Teams for remote coordination and collaboration.
Proficiency reviewing and commenting on drawings and technical submittals in Bluebeam.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Master of Science in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, or related discipline.
Experience with hyperscale data center design for major global clients or similar organizations.
Deep familiarity with direct liquid cooling (DLC), high-density AI/GPU deployments, and associated control, monitoring, leak detection, and operational management systems.
Commissioning experience and/or relevant certifications such as Certified Automation Professional (CAP), ISA certifications, cybersecurity certifications, or mission-critical commissioning credentials.
Experience designing and integrating Critical Environment Monitoring Systems (CEMS), Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) platforms, Energy Management Systems (EMS), and Operational Technology (OT) cybersecurity architectures.
Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams to deliver commitments on schedule and within budget while meeting quality and client expectations.
Familiarity with advanced analytics, digital twins, predictive maintenance technologies, machine learning-based operational optimization, and enterprise-scale data center monitoring platforms.

Work Environment

Primarily office-based with 25–50% field travel; active construction site environments require PPE compliance and site safety plan adherence.
Collaborative EPC delivery environment with close coordination across MEP, structural, civil, and program management teams and regular engagement with Global Integrated

Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. new_jobs.title: Senior Officer, AI Platform Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General, and has its Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. IFRC has five regional offices in Africa, Asia Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas. IFRC also has country cluster delegations and country delegations throughout the world. Together, the Geneva Headquarters and the field structure (regional, cluster and country) comprise the IFRC Secretariat.

IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

Background to the position

In virtually all countries, people increasingly rely on and expect a diverse range of digital services (e.g., through their mobile devices) to interact with local government, companies, and community organizations and services. This disruption is already happening to humanitarian assistance. Yet, the Digital Divide remains a persistent and significant challenge at both national and local levels.

The need for a successful and large-scale digital transformation is urgent. And Digitally Transforming the IFRC and its 191 members is a complex process which requires collaborative action and support across the membership. Therefore, the IFRC recently developed a Digital Transformation Strategy which was approved by the IFRC Governing Board in May 2021.  

The Digital Transformation Department (DTD) has full leadership responsibility for the implementation of the digital transformation strategy and the positive impact it will have on the 191 National Society members of the IFRC. The DTD provides strategic leadership and guides the IFRC Secretariat as well as the members network to adapt and innovate humanitarian services, drawing on digital services, data-enabled decision-making, and other opportunities for digital transformation in support of the IFRC’s Strategy 2030. In addition, the DTD is responsible for the development and implementation of business transformation, information technology and digitalization services throughout the IFRC Secretariat, thereby supporting the same transformation in 191 NSs, setting the vision, and drawing stakeholders together on this digital journey. 

Job Purpose

The incumbent reports to the AI and Data management unit (“AI & Data unit”), that is accountable to the Director of the DTD. The other units and teams reporting to the DT Director include the Enterprise Architecture, Strategy & Planning unit, the Digital development and management unit, the Infrastructure & Security Team and the Global Service Desk and Endpoint Management team. Under the leadership of the Director, these units and teams serve as members of the global DTD management team, along with the CISO and Regional DT managers.

The AI & Data unit is responsible to deliver greater value from IFRC’s data, and ensures the development and implementation of IFRCs data and AI governance and strategy, in close collaboration with the IFRC’s Data Protection Office and through indirect management of data professionals in other departments. The unit oversees all data operations, data product lifecycles and manages the organisation’s data platform, as well as the coordination and support to AI initiatives.

The Senior Officer, AI Platform Engineering will also interact with internal and external AI and data experts, private sector, academia, external suppliers, vendors and consultants who are sourced to deliver AI-related activities.

Job Purpose

The Senior Officer, AI Platform Engineering builds and runs the shared platform that IFRC teams use to create AI solutions on Microsoft technologies. The role provisions and operates Azure AI services, supports colleagues who build agents in Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 Copilot, and makes it easy for teams to build AI that is secure, compliant and affordable.

The role puts into practice the IFRC security and governance standards, and works closely with developers, data protection colleagues and IT operations across the Secretariat.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Azure AI Platform Operations
Operate and maintain IFRC's Microsoft-based AI platforms and services (e.g. Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI and related Azure services, Copilot Studio and Power Platform) across development, testing and production environments.
Configure and maintain platform components and integrations to support the deployment and operation of AI applications and services.
Develop and maintain version-controlled infrastructure-as-code templates for AI platform resources, automate environment provisioning and identify and remediate configuration drift against approved baselines.
Manage model deployments, quotas and capacity, and track model retirements so that applications keep working when models are updated or withdrawn.
Ensure proper life-cycle management of AI related services.
Monitor platform availability, performance, resource utilization and operational costs, identifying opportunities for optimization.
Maintain resource tagging and usage attribution by team or solution, configure budget and abnormal-consumption alerts, provide cost and capacity forecasts, and coordinate the removal or resizing of unused resources with their owners.
Operate the AI gateway in Azure API Management, including authentication, rate limits per team, load balancing, and usage logging.
Troubleshoot platform and deployment issues, investigate incidents and implement corrective actions within the scope of the role.
Support for developers and makers
Build and maintain reusable templates, reference architectures and code samples for common patterns, such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents built with Foundry Agent Service or the Microsoft Agent Framework.
Support colleagues building AI applications and agents in Azure AI Foundry, building agents in Copilot Studio and extending Microsoft 365 Copilot, including environment setup, connectors and publishing.
Build and maintain the pipelines that connect AI services to IFRC data in SharePoint, Microsoft Fabric, Dataverse and other sources.
Onboard new teams to the platform, answer their technical questions and keep its documentation clear and current.
Collaborates with the team in developing and providing to the organization trainings and learning materials related to AI with a focus on platform and security.

Job Duties And Responsibilities (continued)

AI Workload Operations and Security
Build, maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines for AI applications and related platform components, including version control, automated testing, deployment and release management.
Develop and apply established operational practices for managing AI workloads, including appropriate resource allocation and environment configuration.
Implement established security configurations and operational procedures for AI workloads.
Implement and maintain approved Azure Policy and network security guardrails for AI services, including permitted deployment regions, private connectivity, restrictions on public access and approved authentication methods; monitor compliance and track exceptions through the agreed review process.
Monitor relevant Azure security alerts and recommendations affecting AI workloads (e.g. Defender for Cloud) and coordinate follow-up actions.
Apply established identity and access management practices for applications and workloads, including secure credential and secrets management using Azure Key Vault and Microsoft Entra ID.
Prepare the technical evidence needed for the release review of AI agents and services, and put agreed controls in place before go-live.
Support the implementation of data protection and security controls for AI solutions, including relevant Microsoft Purview configurations.
Contribute to technical security assessments and incident investigations related to AI workloads.
Configure Power Platform environments and data loss prevention (DLP) policies for Copilot Studio.
Documentation and Collaboration
Maintain technical documentation of Azure AI platforms and solutions, including deployment configurations, integrations, dependencies, operational procedures, data sources and data flows.
Collaborate with AI developers, data professionals and other technical stakeholders to ensure the reliable deployment and operation of AI solutions.
Ensure that AI platforms and workloads align with IFRC's infrastructure, security and operational standards.
Act as the first technical point of contact for operational questions and issues related to Azure AI platforms and deployed solutions.
Stay up to date with developments in Azure cloud technologies, platform engineering, DevOps and AI operations, and identify opportunities to improve platform reliability, automation, performance, cost efficiency and existing processes.

Duties applicable to all staff

Work actively towards the achievement of IFRC’s goals.
Abide by and work in accordance with the Red Cross and Red Crescent principles.
Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.

Education

Required

Degree in in computer science, information security, data science, or related field.

Preferred

Relevant Microsoft certifications, such as Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), Azure AI App and Agent Developer Associate (AI-103) or the earlier Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102), DevOps Engineer Expert (AZ-400) or Cloud and AI Security Engineer Associate (SC-500).

Experience

Required

Minimum 5 years of experience in cloud operations, DevOps, platform engineering or a related technical field.
Hands-on experience operating and maintaining applications and services in Microsoft Azure environments.
Experience developing and maintaining infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Bicep, Terraform) and automating environment provisioning.
Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (e.g. Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions) and managing deployment and release processes in production environments.
Experience with scripting and automation using Python and/or PowerShell
Experience with cloud monitoring, logging and troubleshooting tools (e.g. Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights).

Preferred

Experience operating or supporting AI/ML or generative AI applications in production environments.

At Jacobs, we never settle — we push boundaries, elevate standards, and deliver with purpose. As a senior subject matter expert (SME) within our Data Center team, you’ll lead I&C engineering efforts across a portfolio of data center projects, including new builds and retrofits. As part of the vision of the I & C SME, you’ll drive the technical direction and ensure controls solutions meet the highest standards of performance and constructability.

You’ll serve as a key technical leader, guiding a portfolio of projects and coordinating closely with interdisciplinary engineering teams. You will mentor I&C leads and support the projects by meeting with clients and upper management as required, with the ability to speak directly to the status of various projects. Your expertise will shape project execution, influence design strategy, and strengthen our delivery excellence.

Your guidance will shape both design delivery and our Design-Build delivery methodology across a fast-growing hyperscale project portfolio.

Key Contributions

Provide quality reviews of complex projects spanning building automation systems (BAS), industrial control systems (ICS), SCADA, EPMS, and critical facility monitoring and control platforms for hyperscale data center facilities.

Develop and validate advanced control sequences, network communication architectures, and system integration strategies; establish controls design standards and mentor team members in best-practice automation, instrumentation, and controls engineering techniques.
Oversee critical calculations and analyses related to instrumentation sizing and selection, control valve applications, sensor accuracy and reliability, network capacity, alarm management, and controls integration; provide technical governance for schedules, design documentation, and interdisciplinary coordination.

Partner with mechanical, electrical, civil, structural, and commissioning disciplines to ensure seamless integration of instrumentation and control systems throughout the project lifecycle, from concept design through commissioning, startup, and turnover.

At Jacobs, the world’s No. 1 design firm, you’ll lead industry-defining data center and advanced manufacturing projects with global impact.

Knowledge of CAD and BIM platforms including Revit.
Knowledge and application of relevant industry standards and codes, including NFPA 70 (NEC), NFPA 72, NFPA 110, ISA-5.1, ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Standards, ASHRAE Guideline 36, ASHRAE TC 9.9 recommendations, Uptime Institute guidance, and other data center industry standards.

Proficiency reviewing and commenting on drawings and technical submittals in Bluebeam.

Master of Science in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, or related discipline.
